verses.text: "Go up and down the streets of Jerusalem. Look around and think about it. Search through its town squares. If you can find even one person who acts fairly and looks for the truth, I will forgive this city.
Even when they say, 'As surely as the LORD lives,' they are still making false promises."

LORD, do your eyes not look for truth? You struck them, but they felt no pain. You crushed them, but they refused to accept correction. They made their faces harder than rock. They refused to turn back.
I thought, "These are only the poor. They are foolish, for they do not know the way of the LORD or the law of their God.
I will go to the leaders and speak to them. Surely they know the way of the LORD and the law of their God." But all of them together had broken the yoke and torn off the chains.

So a lion from the forest will attack them. A wolf from the desert will destroy them. A leopard will wait outside their towns to tear to pieces anyone who comes out. For their rebellions are many, and they have turned away from God again and again.

"Why should I forgive you? Your children have left me and made promises by gods that are not gods at all. I gave them all they needed, yet they committed adultery and crowded into the houses of prostitutes.
They are like well fed stallions, full of desire. Each one neighs for his neighbor's wife.
Should I not punish them for this?" says the LORD. "Should I not take revenge on a nation like this?
Go through her vineyards and destroy them, but do not destroy them completely. Strip off her branches, for these people do not belong to the LORD.
For the people of Israel and the people of Judah have been completely unfaithful to me," says the LORD.
They have lied about the LORD and said, "He will do nothing! No harm will come to us. We will never see war or hunger.
The prophets are just wind. The word of God is not in them. Let what they say happen to them!"
So this is what the LORD God of Armies says: "Because the people have said this, I will make my words in your mouth a fire, and these people the wood, and the fire will burn them up.
People of Israel," says the LORD, "I am bringing a nation from far away against you, a strong and ancient nation, a people whose language you do not know, whose words you cannot understand.
Their arrows bring death like an open grave. All of them are mighty warriors.

They will eat up your harvest and your food. They will eat up your sons and daughters. They will eat up your flocks and herds. They will eat up your vines and fig trees. With the sword they will destroy the walled cities you trust in.
Yet even in those days," says the LORD, "I will not destroy you completely.

When the people ask, 'Why has the LORD our God done all these things to us?' you will tell them, 'As you have left me and served foreign gods in your own land, so now you will serve foreigners in a land that is not yours.'
Announce this to the people of Jacob and tell it in Judah:
Listen to this, you foolish people who have no sense, who have eyes but do not see, who have ears but do not hear.

Should you not fear me?" says the LORD. "Should you not tremble before me? I made the sand a border for the sea, a boundary that lasts forever, which it cannot cross. The waves may toss, but they cannot win. They may roar, but they cannot cross it.
But these people have stubborn and rebellious hearts. They have turned aside and gone away.
They do not say to themselves, 'Let us respect the LORD our God, who gives the autumn and spring rains at the right time, and who makes sure we have the weeks of harvest.'
Your sins have kept these good things away. Your wrongdoing has kept you from having good things.
Among my people are wicked people who lie in wait like hunters hiding to catch birds. They set traps to catch people.
Like cages full of birds, their houses are full of things they got by lying. That is how they have become powerful and rich.
They have grown fat and sleek. There is no limit to their evil deeds. They do not defend the cause of the orphan so that it may succeed. They do not stand up for the rights of the poor.
Should I not punish them for this?" says the LORD. "Should I not take revenge on a nation like this?
A shocking and horrible thing has happened in the land.
The prophets tell lies, and the priests rule by their own power. And my people love it this way! But what will you do when the end comes?"
